rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding parallels in 39:52 and 40:82–83 confirm that Qarun means know-how for acquiring wealth, as explained earlier.
rows.anchor: وعرض الآيات على قصة قارون لا يبقي شكا في أن المراد بالعلم في كلامه ما قدمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying he was given wealth without naming God as giver, Qarun turns away from mentioning God and disparages divine majesty.
rows.anchor: من غير إسناد الإيتاء إلى الله سبحانه كما في قول الناصحين له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes Qarun with the simplest refutation: stronger, more numerous earlier peoples also had wealth by their own knowledge, yet God destroyed them for sin; if knowledge secured wealth and safety, they would have survived and kept it.
rows.anchor: استفهام توبيخي وجواب عن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context this describes God's practice of punishing criminals without delay or hearing fabricated excuses: He knows the facts and brings an irresistible punishment suddenly, unlike human rulers who question offenders.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن المراد به بيان السنة الإلهية في تعذيب المجرمين وإهلاكهم بذنوبهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the knowledge to be Torah learning, since Qarun was the most learned Israelite in the Torah.
rows.anchor: فقيل المراد بالعلم في قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the knowledge as alchemy, which Qarun learned from Moses, Joshua son of Nun, and Caleb son of Jephunneh; he alone possessed it.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد علم الكيمياء وكان قد تعلمه من موسى ويوشع بن نون وكالب بن يوقنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says Qarun knew how to extract buried treasures and had brought out many such treasures.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالعلم علم استخراج الكنوز والدفائن وقد استخرج به كنوزا ودفائن كثيرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the knowledge as God's knowledge and the gift as a special divine choice of Qarun; عندي expresses what he thought.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالعلم علم الله تعالى والمعنى أوتيته على علم من الله وتخصيص منه قصدني به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view also takes knowledge as God's knowledge, but in the sense of what He knew: the gift was based on good He knew to be in Qarun.
rows.anchor: وقيل العلم علم الله لكنه بمعنى المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across these interpretations, على can indicate superiority; some also allow it to mean because of or on account of.
rows.anchor: على جميع هذه الأقوال للاستعلاء وجوز أن تكون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading places the negated question at Judgment: it is not an inquiry for information, since God knows their sins and angels know them from records and their marks; 37:24 is questioning for reproach instead.
rows.anchor: سؤال يوم القيامة والمنفي سؤال الاستعلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A proposed reconciliation gives the question the same sense in both passages, but says it occurs at one Judgment station and is absent at another.
rows.anchor: ويمكن إن يكون السؤال في الآيتين بمعنى واحد والنفي والإثبات باعتبار اختلاف المواقف يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to the stronger people destroyed earlier and takes the criminals as different people, who are not asked about those earlier people's sins.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالمجرمين غيرهم والمعنى لا يسأل عن ذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative readings of the question do not fit the immediate context, which completes the rebuke of Qarun's claim that his knowledge made him wealthy.
rows.anchor: وهذه كلها وجوه من التفسير لا يلائمها السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حظ means a share of happiness or good fortune.
rows.anchor: الحظ هو النصيب من السعادة والبخت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They make worldly life the goal of every effort and know nothing beyond it, including the afterlife's reward; this is the limit of their knowledge in 53:29–30, so they treat Qarun's wealth as unqualified happiness.
rows.anchor: أي يجعلونها الغاية المطلوبة في مساعيهم ليس لهم وراءها غاية فهم على جهل من الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويل denotes ruin and is used either to invoke ruin or to deter from something disapproved; here it rebukes the wish for Qarun's wealth.
rows.anchor: الويل الهلاك ويستعمل للدعاء بالهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are believers who know God, addressing ignorant people who wished for Qarun's wealth and called it absolute happiness.
rows.anchor: والقائلون بهذا القول هم المؤمنون أهل العلم بالله يخاطبون به أولئك الجهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reward is better than Qarun's riches for believers who do good; if the wishers are believers and righteous, they should wish for that reward.
rows.anchor: ومرادهم أن ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا مما أوتي قارون فإن كانوا مؤمنين صالحين فليتمنوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talaqqiya means conveying or making understood, while talaqqi means understanding and receiving.
rows.anchor: والمعنى وما يفهم هذه الكلمة

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: On one reported reading, the pronoun refers to the implied statement that God's reward is better, and only the patient grasp it.
rows.anchor: والضمير - على ما قالوا - للكلمة المفهومة من السياق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the way or practice, and receiving it means understanding it or being enabled to follow it.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير للسيرة أو الطريقة ومعنى تلقيها فهمها أو التوفيق للعمل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient are those who endure hardship, keep to obedience, and resist sins.
rows.anchor: والصابرون هم المتلبسون بالصبر عند الشدائد وعلى الطاعات وعن المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only people patient with self-restraint can truly believe the afterlife's reward surpasses worldly gain, since faith and righteous action require resisting desires and surrendering many pleasures.
rows.anchor: لا يتحقق إلا ممن له صفة الصبر على مرارة مخالفة الطبع وعصيان النفس الأمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both pronouns refer to Qarun, and the sinking follows from his wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: الضميران لقارون والجملة متفرعة على بغيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A فئة is a group whose members gravitate toward one another; victory and resistance carry the sense of protection and holding off harm.
rows.anchor: الفئة الجماعة يميل بعضهم إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No group could shield Qarun from punishment and he could not resist it; his wealth and strength, supposedly gained by knowledge, failed without God and showed God had granted his riches.
rows.anchor: فما كان له جماعة يمنعونه العذاب وما كان من الممتنعين على خلاف ما كان يظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء makes the lack of rescuers a consequence of the sinking: the event exposes Qarun's false claims of deserving wealth and independence from God.
rows.anchor: لتفريع الجملة على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word وي is reported to express regret and sometimes wonder; either sense fits, though regret comes to mind first here.
rows.anchor: كلمة تندم وربما تستعمل للتعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers admit Qarun was wrong: abundance and scarcity come by God's will, not human genius or management; their كأن signals the start of doubt in a claim they had previously accepted.
rows.anchor: اعتراف منهم ببطلان ما كان يزعمه قارون وهم يصدقونه أن القوة والجمع في الدنيا بنبوغ الإنسان في علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their next words, stated with certainty, show they now know God could have caused them to sink too, confirming that كأن marks emerging doubt rather than real uncertainty about providence.
rows.anchor: { لولا أن من الله علينا لخسف بنا } على طريق الجزم والتحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their second وي expresses renewed regret and withdraws the desire that they had occupied Qarun's place.
rows.anchor: تندم منهم ثانيا وانتزاع مما كان لازم تمنيتهم مكان قارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the Hereafter and its people is the conclusion drawn from Qarun's story.
rows.anchor: الآية وما بعدها بمنزلة النتيجة المستخرجة من القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distant demonstrative highlights the Hereafter's honor, radiance, and lofty status; it means the blessed abode, commonly understood as Paradise.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إليها بلفظ البعيد للدلالة على شرفها وبهائها وعلو مكانتها وهو الشاهد على أن المراد بها الدار الآخرة السعيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reserves the Hereafter for those who do not seek arrogance over His servants or corruption through disobedience; divine law follows human nature and the best social order, so every sin causes earthly corruption directly or indirectly.
rows.anchor: وإرادة العلو هو الاستعلاء والاستكبار على عباد الله وإرادة الفساد فيها ابتغاء معاصي الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that Qarun arranged a false accusation of adultery against Moses; after the woman confessed the plot, Moses commanded the earth to swallow Qarun and his people despite their pleas, and God said He would have answered them had they called Him. Ibn Abbas identifies this as the sinking in the verse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وذلك قوله تعالى { فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض }

rows.speaker: ابن نوفل الهاشمي
rows.claim: A version transmitted by Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim says the woman was brought before Qarun and Israel to accuse Moses, but confessed the truth; Moses complained to God, who empowered him over Qarun.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرزاق وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن نوفل الهاشمي القصة لكن فيها أن المرأة

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi's version says Moses brought Qarun the zakat ruling, Qarun mocked and expelled him, and Moses complained to God, who caused Qarun and his house to sink.
rows.anchor: وروى القمي في تفسيره في القصة أن موسى عليه السلام جاء إلى قارون وبلغه حكم الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls the al-Qummi report mawquf and containing objectionable matters, which is why he leaves it unquoted; the Ibn Abbas and Ibn Nawfal reports are also mawquf.
rows.anchor: والرواية موقوفة مشتملة على أمور منكرة ولذلك تركنا نقلها كما إن روايتي ابن عباس وابن نوفل أيضا موقوفتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ibn Abbas story centers on Qarun's wrongdoing against Moses, whereas the Qur'anic account says he wronged the Israelites; the verse also points to learned, acquired know-how, apparently the means of making wealth.
rows.anchor: على أن رواية ابن عباس تقصص بغيه على موسى عليه السلام والذي تقصه الآيات بغيه على بنى إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present Torah recounts the rebellion differently, naming Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and On with 250 leaders who oppose Moses; the cited account is Numbers chapter 16.
rows.anchor: ففي الإصحاح السادس عشر من سفر العدد وأخذ قورح بن بصهار بن نهات بن لاوي وداثان وأبيرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the opening says trial is an inescapable divine practice, the sura recalls seven earlier prophets and their tested peoples: some were saved and others destroyed; the first three stories mention both outcomes, the last four only destruction.
rows.anchor: أن الفتنة سنة إلهية لا معدل عنها

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses طوفان as abundant, engulfing water because its volume surrounds the land.
rows.anchor: في المجمع الطوفان الماء الكثير الغامر لأنه يطوف بكثرته في نواحي الأرض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another definition extends طوفان to anything that sweeps over something with abundance and force, such as flood, wind, or darkness, though water is the usual usage.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو كل ما يطوف بالشيء على كثرة وشدة من السيل والريح والظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying a thousand years less fifty instead of nine hundred and fifty years intensifies and magnifies the duration.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما دون أن يقال تسعمائة وخمسين سنة للتكثير

words: فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is that 950 years was Noah's mission, from his commissioning until the Flood, unlike the present Torah's account of this as his lifespan; this was discussed under Noah in the commentary on Hud.
rows.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في أن الألف إلا خمسين مدة دعوة نوح عليه السلام ما بين بعثته إلى أخذ الطوفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved Noah and those aboard with him: his family and a small number of believers, who were not wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: أي فأنجينا نوحا وأصحاب السفينة الراكبين معه فيها وهم أهله وعدة قليلة من المؤمنين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in made it a sign most likely refers to the event or the rescue; referring it to the ship is strained.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الضمير للواقعة أو للنجاة وأما رجوعه إلى السفينة فلا يخلو من بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worlds here are the many different communities of later generations.
rows.anchor: والعالمين الجماعات الكثيرة المختلفة من الأجيال اللاحقة بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is grammatically coordinated with Noah, meaning that God also sent Abraham to his people.
rows.anchor: معطوف على قوله { نوحا } أي وأرسلنا إبراهيم إلى قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In light of the following verses, Abraham's call to worship God and fear Him is a summons to monotheism and a warning, with worship restricted to God.
rows.anchor: دعوة إلى التوحيد وإنذار بقرينة الآيات التالية فتفيد الجملة فائدة الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even without an explicit word of exclusivity, the command implies worship of God alone: idolaters worship intermediaries such as angels and jinn, believing God can only be approached through them.
rows.anchor: على أن الوثنية لا يعبدون الله سبحانه وإنما يعبدون غيره زعما منهم أنه تعالى لا يمكن أن يعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أوثان is the plural of وثن, meaning an idol.
rows.anchor: الأوثان جمع وثن بفتحتين وهو الصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إفك is something turned away from its true direction, whether a statement or an act.
rows.anchor: والإفك الأمر المصروف عن وجهه قولا أو فعلا

words: إِنَّمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْثَٰنًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols merely idols exposes the falsehood of their worship and makes clear that true worship belongs to God alone; the indefinite plural belittles them as empty claims to divinity.
rows.anchor: { أوثانا } منكر للدلالة على وهن أمرها وكون ألوهيتها دعوى مجردة لا حقيقة وراءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fabricate falsehood by naming idols gods and worshiping them; a God worthy of worship exists, but He is the one God, not the idols.
rows.anchor: أي وتفتعلون كذبا بتسميتها آلهة وعبادتها بعد ذلك فهناك إله تجب عبادته لكنه هو الله الواحد

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People worship idols as intermediaries to attract benefit and provision, but idols cannot provide it: God created both people and their provision, and ownership follows creation.
rows.anchor: إنما تعبدونهم لجلب النفع وهو أن يرضوا عنكم فيرزقوكم ويدروا عليكم الرزق لكنهم ليسوا يملكون لكم رزقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone owns provision, people should seek it from Him, worship Him rather than idols, and thank Him for His many blessings; the benefactor must be thanked.
rows.anchor: فاطلبوا الرزق من عند الله لأنه هو الذي يملكه فلا تعبدوهم بل اعبدوا الله واشكروا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God explains worship and gratitude, shifting their motive from worldly provision to judgment: natural causes govern provision, but faith and worship determine afterlife happiness.
rows.anchor: ولذا جيء بالفصل من غير عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading keeps the warning within Abraham's speech: denial is expected as a recurring custom of idolatrous peoples, but earlier deniers did not escape God's punishment, and the same applies to his people.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه من تمام كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take this as God's direct address to the Quraysh polytheists; al-Tabataba'i considers that unlikely.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنه خطاب منه تعالى لمشركي قريش ولا يخلو من بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the point may be that earlier nations' denial brought God's punishment and could not overcome Him, so the Quraysh will fare likewise; the messenger's duty is only clear delivery under either reading.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يكون المراد أن حالكم في تكذيبكم كحال الأمم من قبلكم لم ينفعهم تكذيبهم شيئا

words: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْخَلْقَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following five divine verses interrupt Abraham's story to prove resurrection and remove its implausibility, since denial of resurrection is central to rejecting the messengers, as Abraham's preceding words indicate.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية إلى تمام خمس آيات من كلامه تعالى واقعة في خلال القصة تقيم الحجة على المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion cites Abraham's being chosen in this life and counted among the righteous in the next, a passage treated earlier in volume one and identified as 2:130.
rows.anchor: ولقد اصطفيناه في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين البقرة 130 في الجزء الأول من الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elliptical opening means either We sent Lot or Remember Lot, when he addressed his people.
rows.anchor: أي وأرسلنا لوطا أو واذكر لوطا إذ قال لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's statement reports their indecency as an expression of astonishment and condemnation; the indecency is sex between males.
rows.anchor: { إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة } إخبار بداعي الاستعجاب والإنكار

words: مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains and reinforces the indecency: this act had not become widespread among any earlier people, or the clause describes the subject of their act.
rows.anchor: استئناف يوضح معنى الفاحشة ويؤكده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic lām and nūn mark a question about conduct no sensible listener would credit or accept.
rows.anchor: استفهام من أمر من الحري أن لا يصدقه سامع ولا يقبله ذو لب ولذا أكد بالنون واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context points to abandoning the path of procreation by choosing men instead of women; cutting the road is a figure for turning away from women and marriage.
rows.anchor: إهمال طريق التناسل وإلغاؤها وهي إتيان النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A النادي is a meeting place only when its people are gathered; the people of Lot publicly committed sexual obscenities or their vile preliminaries there.
rows.anchor: والنادي هو المجلس الذي يجتمعون فيه ولا يسمى ناديا إلا إذا كان فيه أهله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported alternative says they robbed and assaulted travelers passing their town, pelting them, taking property, having sex with them, and charging three dirhams; another says simply that they were highway robbers. The author says the context contradicts this.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بقطع السبيل قطع سبيل المارة بديارهم فإنهم كانوا يفعلون هذا الفعل بالمجتازين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view lists many vices in their assemblies, including insults, gambling, pelting passersby, music, nudity, and sodomy; al-Tabataba'i says context indicates the specific sexual conduct already described.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بإتيان المنكر في النادي أن مجالسهم كانت تشتمل على أنواع المنكرات والقبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sarcastic demand for God's punishment mocks Lot and shows that he had warned them of a punishment; another passage in their story says so.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من جوابهم أنه كان ينذرهم بعذاب الله

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A long report in al-Tawhid, attributed to Ali and answering a question about apparent scriptural conflicts, says kufr here means disavowal, with people disowning one another; it compares Satan's disavowal in 14:22 and Abraham's in 60:4.
rows.anchor: في التوحيد عن علي عليه السلام في حديث طويل يجيب فيه عما سئل من تهافت الآيات وفيه والكفر في هذه الآية البراءة

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur cites Ibn Mardawayh from Jabir: the Prophet forbade khadhf, identifying it with the wrongdoing in Lot's people's council.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نهى عن الخذف وهو قول الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The same explanation is reported through several compilers from Umm Hani: Lot's people sat by the road pelting passersby and mocking them.
rows.anchor: عن أم هاني بنت أبي طالب ولفظ الحديث قالت سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن قول الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Kafi, Abu Abd Allah recounts that Abraham repeatedly asks the angels how many righteous residents would spare Lot's town; they promise to save Lot and his family, except his wife. Hasan ibn Ali reads Abraham's bargaining as an effort to preserve them, linked to 11:74.
rows.anchor: في الكافي بإسناده عن أبي زيد الحماد عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث نزول الملائكة على إبراهيم بالبشرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is a stable, purposeful order, not play; creation and governance are inseparable and belong to God. Everything else is created, owned, and dependent, so nothing can independently manage itself or anything else.
rows.anchor: فخلق السماوات والأرض على نظام ثابت لا يتغير وسنة إلهية جارية لا تختلف ولا تتخلف
